standard_prerequisites.name: First-quadrant spectral sequence
standard_prerequisites.use: Spectral sequence of the double complexes.

core_obligations: Choose a quasi-isomorphism F^• → I^• into a bounded below complex of injectives, which is K-injective; the internal-hom construction represents R SheafHom(E^•,F^•) by the product complex H'^•, and the products equal direct sums because only finitely many terms are nonzero (proof lines 11902-11914).

Both H^• and H'^• are total complexes of double complexes; the first-quadrant spectral sequence reduces the quasi-isomorphism to the iso H^p(SheafHom_{O_X}(E, F^•)) → H^p(SheafHom_{O_X}(E, I^•)) on cohomology sheaves for E a direct summand of a finite free module (proof lines 11915-11931).

For E finite free the iso is clear (componentwise direct sums); the summand case follows by additivity since SheafHom(E,-) is a direct summand of SheafHom(G,-) for G = E ⊕ E' finite free (proof lines 11932-11945).
proof_roadmap: Use bounded-below injectives and finite products as sums.
Spectral sequence reduction to one module.
Free case by inspection, summand case by additivity.
difficulty_reason: Bounded-below injective resolutions are K-injective and the products become finite direct sums; the double-complex spectral sequence reduces to the cohomology iso for a single summand of a finite free module, which follows from the free case by additivity.
